Hi Alex,

Thanks again for a great demo last week. Stellar is ready to move forward with the expansion we discussed — we want to extend the term and add capacity in the same paperwork rather than do two separate transactions. High level asks:

- Term: move from 12 months to 24 months with aligned renewal on Nov 1, 2030
- Capacity: baseline from 1.5M tokens/month to 6M tokens/month (burst to 10M)
- Pricing: prefer tiered usage discount starting at +3M tokens/month
- Compliance: include specific data deletion language for our EU transits and an SLA credit cap for partial outages

Attached a stub order form (Stellar_OrderForm_v3.pdf) showing quantities and suggested pricing. Can your team update the MSA redline to reflect the term change and add an Exhibit for the new capacity schedule? Procurement will need a version that goes to legal on our side.

We'd like to close by May 15 if possible.

Best,
Jordan
VP, Cloud Platforms
Stellar Manufacturing

Alex / team / Jordan — attaching a redline of the MSA (MSA_amendment_redline_20290503.docx) and a short commentary below on the decisions we made.

Summary of redline decisions:
- Term mechanics: we propose a 24-month initial term that begins on the Effective Date (signature on the order form). If Stellar prefers Nov 1 start, we can align the Effective Date but will need to confirm proration and billing implications.
- Termination: preserved customer termination for convenience at 60 days' notice after month 12, with early-termination fee equal to 3 months' committed spend — this is a compromise to balance revenue protection and flexibility for Stellar.
- Data deletion: added an explicit EU transit/data deletion paragraph (Section 5.3) and tied log retention to 90 days by default unless otherwise negotiated; included cross-border transfer note and customer-controlled deletion timing.
- SLA credits: proposed cap at 50% of monthly recurring fees for partial outages up to 72 hours and 100% for total monthly outage; included procedures for credit claims.

Open items (please confirm):
1) Effective Date: signature vs. Nov 1 — procurement needs clarity.
2) Burst policy cap: Ben to propose a simple monthly cap number we can write into Exhibit A.
3) Data residency addendum: Jordan, if Stellar requires a VPC/on-prem package or HSM KMS, we should list as a separate SOW/addendum and note procurement lead times.

If those are OK, I'll produce the clean packet and send to Jordan's procurement with tracked redline comments. Targeting EOD May 4 to meet your May 15 close.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

- Effective Date: we prefer Nov 1 start to align with our fiscal year. Procurement asked for a brief note on proration mechanics; Anika will confirm numbers and get back by COB May 6.
- Burst cap: procurement is comfortable with a monthly hard cap of 10M tokens and agreed overage rate as you proposed.
- Data residency: Stellar does not need a full on-prem deployment but will require documented KMS integration plan; we will accept a separate addendum SOW.

Please do send the consolidated packet to procure@stellarmfg.com and cc me. If we get the packet by EOD May 4 we can route internally and push for signature by May 14. Also please include a DocuSign link for expedited signing.
